---
title: 'Factoring Trust: A Machine-Checked Characterization of Where Verification Must End'
author:
  - name: Timothy DeHerrera
    affiliations:
      - name: Cyphrpunk LLC
    email: timothy@cyphrpunk.com
abstract: |
  Every deployed verification system ships a trusted remainder — a
  certificate authority, a genesis seed, a witness quorum — and the
  literature that studies each such system formalizes what can be
  *established* while leaving the remainder assumed, listed, and never
  analyzed. We give that remainder a shape. Two assumptions are
  irreducible, and we grant them: that the cryptography holds, and that
  the verifier being run is the one that was specified — Thompson's
  trusting-trust attack. Above those two, trust is exactly the
  complement of verifiability, and that complement *factors*.
  Verification of a claim over a growing, append-only record fails for
  exactly one of three reasons: the claim is not determined by the
  record, the record does not certify it at the verifier's computational
  power, or the claim does not survive the record's growth. Each failure
  names whom the verifier must trust and what repairing it costs. The
  "exactly" is derived rather than stipulated — a biconditional
  machine-checked in Lean 4 across a tower of verifier strata (oracle,
  computable; the polynomial stratum remains an open conjecture), whose
  reverse direction constructs the evidence scheme out of the three
  conditions. A companion theorem, the verification ceiling, carries the
  same factoring beyond append-only records to any structure whose
  artifacts are justified by the artifacts they were built from,
  provided the domain can say what record each artifact commits. We
  instantiate it twice from one shared core: a cryptographic identity
  system, whose hash chain is proved to supply those records, and a
  deliberately light source-integrity system, instantiated over a
  content-neutral stand-in instead. Every ingredient of
  this factoring is independently attested in the literature — the
  observables-frame algebra of synthetic topology, CALM's
  monotonicity-coordination biconditional, archival diplomatics'
  empirically tested determination hypothesis — but no source we reached
  composes them, or names their common complement as trust.
date: 2026-07-24
---
